Zdeněk Fierlinger (1891-07-11, Olomouc–1976-05-02) was a Czechoslovak diplomat and politician who served as the prime minister of Czechoslovakia from 1944 to 1946.

 As leader of the London-based Czechoslovak government-in-exile, Fierlinger played a crucial role in the country's post-war reconstruction. However, his close ties with the Soviet Union led to his eventual merger of his Czech Social Democratic Party with the Czechoslovak Communist Party after the communist coup in 1948.

 Despite these changes, Fierlinger remains an important figure in Czechoslovak history, symbolizing the complex relationships between Eastern European nations and the global superpowers of the time.

 His legacy as a political leader from Olomouc continues to be felt today, with many regarding him as a key player in shaping the country's post-war trajectory.

 In the years following his death, Fierlinger's name became synonymous with the tumultuous period of Czechoslovak history that followed World War II, leaving behind a lasting impact on the region's politics and identity.

Zdeněk Fierlinger was a Czechoslovak diplomat and politician who served as the prime minister of Czechoslovakia from 1944 to 1946. He played a key role in shaping the country's post-war government, particularly in his efforts to establish close ties with the Soviet Union. As a leading figure in the Czech Social Democratic Party, Fierlinger was instrumental in facilitating the merger between his party and the Czechoslovak Communist Party after the communist coup in 1948.

Fierlinger's tenure as prime minister was marked by significant economic reforms and infrastructure development projects. He also oversaw the reconstruction of Czechoslovakia's relations with Western powers, paving the way for increased cooperation between the country and the United States and the United Kingdom.

Despite his efforts to maintain a balance between Czechoslovakia's socialist and democratic traditions, Fierlinger's close association with the Soviet Union ultimately led to his downfall. His successor, Klement Gottwald, would go on to implement more radical socialist policies, further cementing Czechoslovakia's ties to the Eastern Bloc.

In recognition of his contributions to Czechoslovak politics, Fierlinger was awarded the Order of the White Lion in 1976, a prestigious honor that reflected his commitment to the country's democratic values and institutions.
